text: The square was crowded. <break time="0.8s" /> With people and animals. <break time="0.8s" /> And the air was full of shouting, laughing. <break time="0.8s" /> And the smell of cattle. <break time="0.8s" /> Farmers bargained for a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> Over every cow and pig. <break time="0.8s" /> Always afraid that someone might cheat them. <break time="0.8s" /> At noon the crowd went to Jourdains inn. <break time="0.8s" /> Where a great fire was roasting. <break time="0.8s" /> Chickens, pigeons, and legs of lamb. <break time="0.8s" /> The diners ate and drank happily. <break time="0.8s" /> Talking loudly. <break time="0.8s" /> About the weather and the harvest. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly a drum sounded. <break time="0.8s" /> In the courtyard. <break time="0.8s" /> And everyone except a few who did not care. <break time="0.8s" /> Ran to the doors and windows. <break time="0.8s" /> The town crier announced that a black leather pocketbook had been lost. <break time="0.8s" /> That morning. <break time="0.8s" /> On the road to Beuzeville. <break time="0.8s" /> It held five hundred francs. <break time="0.8s" /> And some business papers. <break time="0.8s" /> And the finder would receive. <break time="0.8s" /> A reward of twenty francs. <break time="0.8s" /> The owner Maître Houlbrèque of Manneville. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked the finder. <break time="0.8s" /> To bring it to the mayors office or to him. <break time="0.8s" /> As the diners were guessing. <break time="0.8s" /> Who might find it. <break time="0.8s" /> A police officer appeared. <break time="0.8s" /> At the door of the dining room. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked for Maître Hauchecorne of Bréauté. <break time="0.8s" /> And told him that the mayor wished to speak with him. <break time="0.8s" /> At once.
